seedling.description: Days 0-14: Germination through early root development. Light intensity reduced to prevent photoinhibition in newly emerged roots.

vegetative.description: Days 15-60: Rapid leaf/stem/root expansion. Maintain higher water content and EC for vigorous growth. 18/6 photoperiod. Prepare for training (LST/SCROG).

flowering_early.description: Days 0-21 of 12/12 cycle. Transition to 12/12 photoperiod triggers floral initiation. Maintain water content to support initial flower development; begin mild generative steering.

flowering_mid.description: Days 22-42 of 12/12 cycle. Bulking phase; flowers increase in density and size. Reduce substrate water content for generative steering (crop steering). EC may increase if PPFD is high (>1500 umol).

flowering_late.description: Days 43-63 of 12/12 cycle (final 3 weeks). Trichome maturation. Lower water content further for increased terpene/cannabinoid concentration. Monitor RH strictly (<50%) for botrytis prevention. Begin harvest window assessment.

drying.description: Post-harvest: 10-14 days. Branches or whole plants hung in a dark, climate-controlled space at about 60°F/60% RH (15-18°C, 55-62% RH) with gentle air movement and no light.
drying.notes: Ensure active air circulation (2-4 air changes per minute). Monitor for botrytis daily. Do not overdry (<10% bud water content); excessive drying degrades terpenes and cannabinoids.

curing.description: Post-drying: 10-30+ days. Trimmed buds in airtight glass jars at controlled humidity. Burp jars 1-2× daily first week, then reduce frequency.
curing.notes: Airtight glass jars. Water activity (aw) 0.55-0.65 prevents mold and preserves terpenes. Minimum 10 days cure; optimal 21-30 days for flavor/cannabinoid development.

sources: https://www.questclimate.com/ (Humidity and VPD management for cannabis)
https://blog.tsrgrow.com/ (Crop steering irrigation and substrate moisture)
https://www.cannabisbusinesstimes.com/ (Cannabis cultivation research and commercial practices)

notes.vwc_vs_water_tension: Substrate volumetric water content (VWC%) and water tension (pF/kPa) both matter. Plants physiologically respond to tension, not volume. Coco substrate characteristics may require adjustment from these targets based on specific brand and pre-treatment (rinse, buffering, etc.).
notes.ec_scaling: EC targets assume standard NPK-based hydroponic nutrients. Under high PPFD (>1500 umol·m⁻²·s⁻¹) with LED, EC may climb to 8-11+ mS/cm; monitor runoff EC to avoid nutrient accumulation.
notes.perpetual_harvest: To implement a 4-flowering perpetual harvest at home (Minnesota 8-plant cap, 4-flowering limit): maintain 2 mother plants (clones), stagger transitions every 2 weeks, and flip every other week to achieve biweekly harvests.
notes.dark_period_critical: During 12/12 flowering, darkness must be uninterrupted and light-leak free. PAR threshold for disruption: 0.01 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹. Even brief red-light exposure mid-dark can delay or prevent flowering.
notes.botrytis_prevention: RH >50% during late flowering and drying dramatically increases botrytis risk. Active dehumidification and airflow are non-negotiable. Water activity >0.65 during curing is unsafe.
notes.trichome_assessment: Harvest timing determined by trichome color (clear/cloudy/amber) under magnification (10-30×). Computer vision + USB microscope + edge inference (Raspberry Pi) is a viable autonomous harvest-timing aid.

notes: DLI bands are derived as PPFD x photoperiod x 0.0036 so the two never disagree; vegetative PPFD set to the standard 400-600; drying set to the 60°F/60% RH practice (corrected 2026-10-07 by Claude Opus).

CO2 band is 300-1500 ppm for an unenriched tent: under light a ventilated tent draws CO2 below ambient (~350), which is normal; below ~300 photosynthesis is CO2-limited and more air exchange is the fix (2026-10-07).
